translations.text: Thus I was composed by a holy and just man, wise in books, a good author: Aldhelm, a noble poet, who was also exalted among the nobility of the Anglo-Saxons, a bishop in Britain.

I, the book, must now, with toil and weight and with full meaning, [?] of the young one [?] of the sorrowful one [?], again and again, speak the truth and no lies: that abundance was always, and often, a help to him, once in his homeland [?], even more than that which is said to be evil [?].

Also, he whom toil holds must never excuse himself [?] from self-control. Instead he must always pray earnestly for help through the thought of his mind, in the little world, that the Lord, the strong Maker, may give him power on earth, so that from then on he always [the passage breaks off here]
